precepts.text: This is the plague on all that fought against Jerusalem, the controversy of Zion: the Most High fights on our behalf, and their flesh consumes away before their bones can hit the pavement.
precepts.point: We have to walk circumspect, because the time is at hand.

note.label: You Are Hated And In Hell

precepts.text: Violence shall no more be heard in thy land, nor wasting nor destruction within thy borders: no bombs in Tel Aviv, Ashdod or Ashkelon when the rightful people are placed there.
precepts.point: Men shall dwell in it and there shall be no more utter destruction, but Jerusalem shall be safely inhabited: if the people there were the right people there would be no war, because the Messiah must return before we enter the land. That is why they are being blown to hell.

note.label: Edom: The Robbers of thy people revealed past and present

precepts.why:
Zechariah ends the day of the Lord with this: “And men shall dwell in it, and there shall be no more utter destruction; but Jerusalem shall be safely inhabited.” The it is the land. When the Lord returns, men shall dwell in it and there shall be no more destruction. Isaiah says the same: “Violence shall no more be heard in thy land, wasting nor destruction within thy borders”.

That is the time when all Israel, all of us, will be in the land. No bombs in Tel Aviv, no bombs in Ashdod, no bombs in Ashkelon, none of that, once the rightful people are rightfully placed in the land. That is not now. “But thou shalt call thy walls Salvation, and thy gates Praise”, because we will be safe living in them.

So if you are the people of the land, why is the war taking place? The prophecy says there will be no more war and destruction in the land once the Lord returns and we get the land. That means you don't belong there. Prophecy shows the Messiah must return for us to get into the land, not before; that is against prophecy. That is why they are getting blown to hell over there.

What is happening now is the first half of Zechariah 14: all nations gathered against Jerusalem to battle, the city taken, the houses rifled, the women ravished. Jerusalem has become “a burdensome stone for all people”: the Israelis are trying to hold on to this land and expand it, and it is becoming a burdensome stone to them, because they are not the chosen people of God. Only when the Lord's feet stand on the mount of Olives, and he is king over all the earth, is violence no more heard in the land.

precepts.text: Thy people also shall be all righteous and inherit the land for ever: the people over there are not all righteous, so they cannot be the guys.
precepts.point: Men shall dwell in it and there shall be no more utter destruction, but Jerusalem shall be safely inhabited: if the people there were the right people there would be no war, because the Messiah must return before we enter the land. That is why they are being blown to hell.

note.label: Edom: The Robbers of thy people revealed past and present

precepts.why:
Zechariah says that when the Lord is king over all the earth, “Jerusalem shall be safely inhabited.” Isaiah says who will inhabit it: “Thy people also shall be all righteous: they shall inherit the land for ever”.

Are the people over there in Israel today all righteous? No. So they cannot be the guys, because they are not all righteous. That doesn't make any damn sense at all.

Ezekiel confirms it: in the latter years we come “into the land that is brought back from the sword, and is gathered out of many people, against the mountains of Israel, which have been always waste: but it is brought forth out of the nations, and they shall dwell safely all of them.” Is the land still waste today? Yes, it is even worse now. Are the Israelis dwelling safely right now? No. They are in bomb shelters, running and hiding, crying about how unsanitary the shelters are. Where is their God at? On vacation? With Epstein? With Bibi? Where is the great Hashem at?

The righteous people who inherit the land for ever are the ones brought forth out of the nations, gathered by the Lord when he returns. That is why Joel says he pleads “for my people and for my heritage Israel”: my people and my land, not all people. He is coming to save his people and give the land to his people, and they shall be all righteous.

precepts.text: Everyone that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall go up from year to year to worship the King and keep the feast of tabernacles. Christ is not killing everybody; remnants are left.
precepts.point: The glory of Lebanon, the fir, pine, and box, shall beautify the place of my sanctuary; Lebanon and its famous trees belong to the Israelites. The sons of them that afflicted thee shall come bending, and all that despised thee shall bow at the soles of thy feet and call thee the city of the Lord, the Zion of the Holy One of Israel. That is what Revelation 3:9 said. The third temple is under Christ, not under Edom.

note.label: Prophesy From Pain to Peace

precepts.why:
When Revelation says “the nations of them which are saved”, Zechariah gives the thought: “And it shall come to pass, that every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles.”

Everyone that is left. Christ is not killing everybody. There are going to be remnants of people left over from the nations that came against Jerusalem. Those are the “saved” of Revelation 21: the ones left.

And what they do is go up every year to worship the King and keep the feast of tabernacles. That is walking in the light of it: obeying the commandments. That is how the nations serve in Isaiah 60, bringing their wealth and their kings to the gates while Israel is inside. “For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish; yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted.”

precepts.text: Every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles. The nations will be forced to give up their idols.
precepts.point: Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities; thine eyes shall see Jerusalem a quiet habitation, at rest, a tabernacle that shall not be taken down, not one stake removed nor any cord broken. You will never take down Jerusalem again. Psalms 46:4-7, God is in the midst of her, she shall not be moved; the heathen raged, the kingdoms were moved, he uttered his voice, the earth melted; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Psalms 48:1-2, beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, the city of the great King.

note.label: Hope Amid Destruction

precepts.why:
Zechariah shows what it looks like when the nations are subdued: “every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles.”

Those that are left are the ones who came against Jerusalem. These nations are going to be forced to give up their idols and come before the King. Year after year they must go up and keep the feast of tabernacles, the very feast they never kept.

That is why Isaiah 33:19 says “Thou shalt not see a fierce people.” The fierce nations with a stammering tongue will not be fierce any more; what is left of them will be worshipping the King, the Lord of hosts, at Jerusalem.

precepts.text: The day cometh that shall burn as an oven; it shall leave them neither root nor branch.
precepts.point: The day that burneth as an oven leaves neither root nor branch. God will end them with the weapon he let them make.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.why:
The Lord said, “I have created the waster to destroy.” What weapon at that time could have been called the waster? Nothing. Zechariah describes it: “Their flesh shall consume away while they stand upon their feet, and their eyes shall consume away in their holes, and their tongue shall consume away in their mouth.” Could anybody then fathom a weapon that did those things? Malachi shows the day it is fulfilled: “For, behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven”.

The prophets did not know about nuclear weapons and atoms back then. They got these visions and explained them the best they could, and the best way to say it was: the waster. God put it on man to make that instrument, and there will be a day when that plague is fulfilled.

“And all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble”: not just Esau and the other nations, but even rebellious Israel, the ones that do not repent. “And the day that cometh shall burn them up, saith the Lord of hosts, that it shall leave them neither root nor branch.” When you burn something it leaves ashes, but with this waster nothing remains. They show dramatic images, but the body does not survive that heat; whatever ash there is is blown into the atmosphere. You are totally gone.

And here is the beauty of it: God put it in their spirit to make that thing, and he is going to use that same thing to end them. The weapon they feel gave them their power, authority and respect, he will turn against them.

precepts.text: The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, but is longsuffering, not willing that any should perish.
precepts.point: The day that burneth as an oven leaves neither root nor branch. God will end them with the weapon he let them make.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.why:
Zechariah's plague and Malachi's day that burns as an oven are coming, so why has it not come yet? Peter answers: “The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.”

The only reason it tarries is that the Lord is waiting for us. It is not really a set time the way we see it: the time is when that set number is sealed, and God knows when that will be. That is why there is no date for it that we are aware of.

“But the day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night”: when you least suspect it, that is when it comes. “In the which the heavens shall pass away with a great noise, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat”. In those days they could not imagine what that sounded like; it sounded terrifying. Now that we understand it, it is no less terrifying, because we know what those nukes can do.

The Lord stays their hand enough that they do not want to use them. They sign treaties against nuclear proliferation because they know if one fires, the other fires back, and it's a wrap, a zero-sum game, the end of the world as they know it. It is like the game Civilization: it lets you build and use a nuke, but once you use it the game ends, because you destroyed the whole earth. The Lord holds it back while he waits for his people to come to repentance.

precepts.text: The heavens being on fire shall be dissolved, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat.
precepts.point: The day that burneth as an oven leaves neither root nor branch. God will end them with the weapon he let them make.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.why:
Peter says, “Seeing then that all these things shall be dissolved, what manner of persons ought ye to be in all holy conversation and godliness, Looking for and hasting unto the coming of the day of God, wherein the heavens being on fire shall be dissolved, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat?” The heavens will be on fire: what else could he be talking about? It is the waster of Zechariah, flesh consuming away while they stand upon their feet.

We hear all this and say, okay, great, but it should move us. What manner of persons ought we to be? In all holiness and godliness. Paul says the same: “Therefore let us not sleep, as do others; but let us watch and be sober.” Sober means don't drink of the mark of the beast, don't drink her wine, don't be so asleep that you think you're an American and nothing is going to touch you. God has not appointed us to wrath; he does not want his elect to be part of that death and destruction.

Looking for and hasting unto that day means you should be able to look boldly and say, I'm looking for it and I want it to come quickly. It is not the time to be divided in BS and simple issues, but to come together stronger and more united, growing in faith and understanding and applying it.

Don't worry that this place is going to be burned away: “Nevertheless we, according to his promise, look for new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness.” That fire is a baptism by fire that cleanses all the evil and reforms the earth so it is fit for our new forms and for the new kingdom. Thy will be done in earth as it is in heaven: the kingdom is coming down, and this place has to be transformed.

precepts.text: The nations that are left go up yearly to worship the King and keep the feast of tabernacles.
precepts.point: The residue of men seek after the Lord in servitude, and the Gentiles called by his name are those who call themselves Jews and Christians.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
Here is more on how the residue of men will seek after the Lord: “And it shall come to pass, that every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles.”

What do they have to keep? The feast of tabernacles. The nations that are left will worship the King and keep the feast. When is the feast of tabernacles? The seventh month, the fifteenth day. So we are going to have to teach that to the nations: in the seventh month, on the fifteenth day, you go up towards Jerusalem to worship the King and you keep the feast of tabernacles.

That is what it means that the residue of men seek after the Lord. They come up under Israel, learning and keeping God's law, the law they would not keep before. It does not contradict Amos 9:12; it says the same thing. Amos just made it plain, while the way Simeon put it leaves people asking what it means.

precepts.text: The families that will not come up shall have no rain.
precepts.point: The residue of men seek after the Lord in servitude, and the Gentiles called by his name are those who call themselves Jews and Christians.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
There may be some rebellious heathen out there: “And it shall be, that whoso will not come up of all the families of the earth unto Jerusalem to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, even upon them shall be no rain.”

That is judgment. No rain means famine, no rain means dearth, no rain means death. Read on: “And if the family of Egypt go not up, and come not, that have no rain; there shall be the plague, wherewith the Lord will smite the heathen that come not up to keep the feast of tabernacles.”

So when Acts 15 says “That the residue of men might seek after the Lord, and all the Gentiles, upon whom my name is called”, it is not an open door where everyone is equal. The residue of men will seek the Lord in servitude, keeping the feast, and those who refuse get no rain and the plague. And the Gentiles upon whom his name is called, those who call themselves Jews and Christians, God's praise and God's anointed: chains for them.

precepts.text: Living waters go out from Jerusalem, and the Lord shall be king over all the earth.
precepts.point: Sirach names the same rivers as the flow of understanding, and the sea of glass is that clear water in heaven.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“And it shall be in that day, that living waters shall go out from Jerusalem”. That is wisdom going forth from Jerusalem. The wisdom comes down from the Father to Christ, it goes to the leaders, and the leaders issue it throughout the earth. “half of them toward the former sea, and half of them toward the hinder sea: in summer and in winter shall it be.” That means all year round. “And the Lord shall be king over all the earth”. Christ is going to be king over all the earth, and Adam is going to be back as king over the earth.

So when Genesis talks about the garden, it is talking about the heavens, but on the earth also God's glory and wisdom went out. That is why it mentions the Tigris and the other rivers. God had leaders, men set up throughout those regions enforcing his laws. His trees were there on the earth too, on earth as it is in heaven. The living waters out of Jerusalem are how it will be again.

Back in Genesis 2:15, “the Lord God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it.” To dress it and keep it means to rule. Adam ruled the heaven and the earth, and we don't know for how long. He died at 930, but his days only started to be numbered after he sinned. Before that he was immortal, so between Genesis 2 and the temptation in Genesis 3 there could have been hundreds or thousands of years. That is the kingdom of Adam. He had children in the heavens, his firstborn, the twelve tribes, and children on the earth.

precepts.text: This is the plague with which the Lord will smite all the people that fought against Jerusalem, their flesh, eyes, and tongue consuming away while they stand on their feet, which is the ICBM, the intercontinental ballistic missile, the nukes.
precepts.point: He may prepare it, but the just shall put it on and the innocent shall divide the silver; we do not want their Louis Vuitton, Versace, or Hermes bags, we want our kingdom back and the whole earth, because it belongs to us, plus what they took and some.

note.label: Job 27: I Will Not Remove My Integrity From Me

precepts.why:
“Those that remain of him shall be buried in death: and his widows shall not weep.” Those that remain are those left after the Most High brings the bombs: “And this shall be the plague wherewith the Lord will smite all the people that have fought against Jerusalem; Their flesh shall consume away while they stand upon their feet, and their eyes shall consume away in their holes, and their tongue shall consume away in their mouth.”

Flesh consuming away while men stand on their feet is the ICBM, the intercontinental ballistic missile, the nukes. This is the portion of a wicked man with God and the heritage of oppressors, their due reward for their works: Esau, Moab, the Amorites, Ammonites, Jebusites, Hittites, and the Negroites in these last days that come against Israel, and also the wicked of our own people, who get no pass just because they come from the seed of Isaac, Abraham, and Jacob. If his children be multiplied, it is for the sword.

precepts.text: Everyone that is left of the nations that came against Jerusalem shall go up year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and keep the feast of tabernacles, so feast days are kept in the kingdom; those left are those left from the bombs.
precepts.point: He may prepare it, but the just shall put it on and the innocent shall divide the silver; we do not want their Louis Vuitton, Versace, or Hermes bags, we want our kingdom back and the whole earth, because it belongs to us, plus what they took and some.

note.label: Job 27: I Will Not Remove My Integrity From Me

precepts.why:
“And it shall come to pass, that every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles.” Those left are those left from the bombs, the ones Job calls “Those that remain of him”.

So feast days are kept in the kingdom. Everyone left of the nations goes up year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and keep the feast of tabernacles. “And it shall be, that whoso will not come up of all the families of the earth unto Jerusalem to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, even upon them shall be no rain.”

precepts.text: This shall be the plague: their flesh shall consume away while they stand upon their feet, their eyes in their holes and their tongues in their mouth; that is a nuclear bomb. We saw it at Hiroshima and Nagasaki, and the weapons have only got more advanced; the Most High is manipulating that weapon so the earth turns into a microwave.
precepts.point: Their fruit shalt thou destroy from the earth and their seed from among the children of men; Esau is not going to be no more. They imagined a mischievous device which they are not able to perform; the Most High makes their devices of none effect and makes ready his arrows against the face of them.

note.label: Psalm 21: Victory Through the King and the Enemy Destroyed

precepts.why:
The arrows the Most High makes ready against the face of them: “And this shall be the plague wherewith the Lord will smite all the people that have fought against Jerusalem; Their flesh shall consume away while they stand upon their feet, and their eyes shall consume away in their holes, and their tongue shall consume away in their mouth.”

Flesh consuming away while they stand on their feet, eyes in their holes, tongues in their mouth: that is a nuclear bomb. We saw it at Hiroshima and Nagasaki, and the weapons have only got more advanced. The Most High is manipulating that weapon so the earth turns into a microwave.

That is how their fruit is destroyed from the earth and their seed from among the children of men. They imagined a mischievous device, but the Most High makes their devices of none effect and turns his own plague on all that fought against Jerusalem.

precepts.text: The Lord shall go forth and fight against those nations, the enemies He fights against.
precepts.point: Let this be the reward of my adversaries from the Lord, and of them that speak evil against my soul. The adversaries are the nations, and the Lord fights for us against our enemies to save us.

note.label: Psalm 109: Give Myself unto Prayer

precepts.why:
“Then shall the Lord go forth, and fight against those nations, as when he fought in the day of battle.” Those nations are the adversaries of the psalm, the enemies he fights against.

The reward David asks for his adversaries from the Lord is the Lord himself going forth against the nations, as he fought in the day of battle, to save his people.

precepts.text: Their flesh shall consume away while they stand upon their feet, and their eyes shall consume away in their holes, and their tongue shall consume away in their mouth.

note.label: Zechariah 11: The Flock of the Slaughter and the Two Staves

precepts.why:
That that dieth, let it die; and that that is to be cut off, let it be cut off; and let the rest eat every one the flesh of another. The scripture says plainly what the end of this land is. “And this shall be the plague wherewith the Lord will smite all the people that have fought against Jerusalem; Their flesh shall consume away while they stand upon their feet, and their eyes shall consume away in their holes, and their tongue shall consume away in their mouth.”

He will no more pity the inhabitants of the land, and out of their hand he will not deliver them. Knowing what is coming on this land is why keeping the law matters now.

precepts.why: The healing of the nations. “Every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem”: the nations not destroyed when Christ returns; there will be a lot of people left, to pay for their judgment and serve. “Shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles.” “Even upon them shall be no rain”: no rain means drought; the plants don’t grow, the cattle can’t eat, and you die. Everyone will celebrate God’s high holy days, or they will die.

note.label: Zechariah 14: The Day of the Lord Cometh

points: This shall be the plague wherewith the Lord will smite all the people that have fought against Jerusalem; their flesh shall consume away while they stand upon their feet, and their eyes shall consume away in their holes, and their tongue shall consume away in their mouth.
A great tumult from the Lord shall be among them; and they shall lay hold every one on the hand of his neighbour, and his hand shall rise up against the hand of his neighbour.
Judah also shall fight at Jerusalem; and the wealth of all the heathen round about shall be gathered together, gold, and silver, and apparel, in great abundance.

note.label: Zechariah 14: The Day of the Lord Cometh

points: Every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles.
Whoso will not come up of all the families of the earth unto Jerusalem to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, even upon them shall be no rain.
This shall be the punishment of Egypt, and the punishment of all nations that come not up to keep the feast of tabernacles.
In that day shall there be upon the bells of the horses, HOLINESS UNTO THE LORD; and every pot in Jerusalem and in Judah shall be holiness unto the Lord of hosts.
In that day there shall be no more the Canaanite in the house of the Lord of hosts.
